subject: Monitoring sampling and customer dashboard entitlement - Velox Retail procurement questions
messages:
From: Alex Tran <alex.tran@veloxretail.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, procurement@veloxretail.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on how SLOs are measured + dashboard access request

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a short questionnaire about the uptime/latency commitments and how you measure them — specifically:

- What exact metric definitions do you use for 'uptime' and for p99 latency? How do you handle retries and client-side timeouts in the measurement?
- Do you sample requests or compute SLOs on every request? If sampling, what's the sampling window and why?
- Is there a way for us to get short-term read-only access to the metrics/dashboard (Grafana or equivalent) to validate the numbers during POC?
- What alerts are generated when a customer route breaches its SLOs and what is the notification cadence?

Procurement prefers a short written answers we can attach to our vendor review; a temporary dashboard link for 30 days would also be ideal. Can you provide that plus any example artifacts?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our internal review meeting is Friday.

Best,
Alex
Alex Tran
Lead SRE, Velox Retail
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tran <alex.tran@veloxretail.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on how SLOs are measured + dashboard access request

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below and I've attached a brief glossary + example CSV that shows how we compute the numbers. Happy to expand any item.

1) Definitions:
- Uptime: percentage of successful API responses from the public API endpoint (2xx) over the selected evaluation window, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and agreed blackout periods.
- p99 latency: 99th percentile of end-to-end server-side response time measured at the edge load balancer in milliseconds. We exclude client-side retries and treat each upstream request once; if a retry hits a different backend we count only the server response that ultimately served the request.

2) Sampling vs full-stream:
- For most customers we compute SLOs from the full stream of request telemetry (no sampling) for the last 30 days by default. For extremely high-volume customers we use deterministic sharding (e.g., 1-in-10) to keep ingestion costs bounded; the shard is stable by request hash to preserve distribution. The attached SLO-Measurement-Examples.csv shows a 7-day and 30-day computation with and without sharding.

3) Dashboard access:
- We can provide a time-limited, read-only Grafana link scoped to your account routes for 30 days. It contains p95/p99 latency, success-rate, error-class breakdown, and per-region node capacity metrics.

4) Alerting/notifications:
- Alerts are generated by our alerting rules on the aggregation layer. For SLO breaches we have:
  * Warning (soft): triggered when rolling p99 or success-rate approaches the threshold (configurable, default: 80% of SLO) — notification to on-call and a webhook to the customer's alerting integration.
  * Breach (hard): triggered when the SLO is violated for the configured evaluation window (e.g., 10 minutes / 1 hour) — immediate page to on-call + email to the customer's primary ops contact.
- We push alerts to PagerDuty, Slack, email, and support webhooks. Notification cadence: on first breach, and then on state changes (resolved, escalated).

Notes and exceptions:
- Scheduled maintenance windows are announced at least 72 hours in advance (console banner + email).
- For customers requiring deeper visibility we can provide a read-only Prometheus endpoint or an aggregated metrics dump under NDA.

Attachments: Monitoring-Glossary.pdf (quick defs), SLO-Measurement-Examples.csv (sample calculations).

If this works, I can create the Grafana invite now — would you like the 30-day link or something shorter? Also looping in Priyom on the sampling/shard policy and Marissa for the dashboard entitlement approval.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Tran <alex.tran@veloxretail.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on how SLOs are measured + dashboard access request

Thanks Mateo — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and SRE:

- For the deterministic sharding you mentioned, what is the effective sample size for a 1-in-10 shard when we expect ~3M requests/day? Will p99 remain stable?
- Can you confirm retention for the raw request telemetry used to compute SLOs (we need at least 30 days for our audit)?
- For the temporary Grafana link: 30 days is fine. Please include instructions to access (we prefer a tokenized link rather than inviting specific emails).

Also, procurement asked whether Redwood will consider a short-term exception to provide per-route 1-min resolution metrics for the POC period (we can sign a DPA amendment). If that's not standard, can you propose an exception path?

Appreciate the quick help.

—Alex
From: priyom_das@redwood.com <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Velox procurement follow-ups — sampling & POC exception request

Marissa — forwarding Velox's follow-ups. Short answers and a suggested exception path below.

- Effective sample size: For 3M req/day a 1-in-10 shard yields ~300k samples/day which is sufficient to stabilize p99 for typical text-generation workloads; however p99 estimates for extremely bursty tail traffic can vary. We recommend 1-in-5 for POC if Velox needs low-noise p99 during their validation window.
- Retention: raw request telemetry retained 90 days by default in our metrics pipeline; aggregated SLO windows retained 13 months. We can provide a 30-day raw telemetry export under NDA.
- Exception path for per-route 1-min resolution: propose a time-limited (30-day) entitlement change — engineering will enable higher cardinality metrics for the Velox route and we will surface a read-only Grafana panel. This requires a brief change request and a cost allocation (small usage fee) for the additional ingestion.

If you approve, Marissa, can we greenlight the 30-day high-resolution POC entitlement and the Grafana token link? I'll draft the short amendment language for procurement.

Thanks,
Priyom
Staff Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tran <alex.tran@veloxretail.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on how SLOs are measured + dashboard access request

Alex — quick update: we've provisioned a 30-day, read-only Grafana link scoped to Velox's account routes and enabled 1-min resolution for the POC period per the proposed exception path. Details below:

- Link (token): https://console.redwood.inference/veloxretail/dashboard/read-only-invite (token delivered in attachment Grafana-invite-link.txt)
- Sampling: POC set to 1-in-5 sharding for high-volume endpoints (see SLO-Measurement-Examples.csv for expected sample counts).
- Retention: telemetry retention unchanged (90 days) — we'll prepare a 30-day export if procurement requires a delivered dump.
- Cost: as discussed, incremental ingestion for 1-min resolution during the 30-day window will be invoiced as a one-off POC usage line item in VEL-2375.

I'll also drop a short amendment for procurement and share the DOCS link. If you want an onboarding call to walk through the panels and alert rules I can schedule one tomorrow morning.

Thanks everyone — happy to help with the amendment language.

Best,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
